correctness.rationale: On the exact domain L,lambda>0, 0<p<=1, all sensor positions in [0,L], the conditional independence model yields equation (1) by direct integration; its center derivative has a strictly positive multiplier and is maximized only at the midpoint. The centered gap derivative factors as positive p*d*exp(-d) times p-exp(-ell/2) H(d), with H strictly increasing, H(0)=1, and exp(-ell/2)H(ell)=(exp(ell)-1)/ell>1. This gives the unique global optimum, with all p and ell boundaries covered. Series inversion yields linear onset, the p=1 small-ell limit yields quarter-points, and logarithmic inversion yields the large-ell law. verify.py independently checked 13036 finite numerical assertions, supplementing rather than replacing the proof. value.rationale: Choosing two wildlife detectors to maximize one-individual encounter probability under incomplete on-site detection is a clear ecological-design question. The proof resolves all unconstrained continuous detector positions, reveals a sharp length-versus-detection-quality frontier, linear separation onset, noncommuting perfect-detection/long-range limits and exact large-habitat thirds. This is an interpretable global design classification rather than a trivial normalization or arbitrary finite calculation; it is not a claim about field practice without calibration.
